back: Nodes with at most two children (left and right); the first node is the root and a node with no children is a leaf.
For every node, keys in the left sub-tree are smaller and keys in the right sub-tree are larger.
Compare with the root, go left if smaller and right otherwise, and repeat until an empty place is found; attach the new node there.
Key, LeftPointer and RightPointer arrays plus RootPointer; 0 means no child.
Pre-order: node, left, right. In-order: left, node, right (sorted order). Post-order: left, right, node.

front: Deleting a leaf or a node with one child
back: A leaf: empty the parent's pointer. One child: the parent points to that child instead.

front: Deleting a node with two children
back: Replace its key with the smallest key of its right sub-tree, then delete that node.
Balanced tree: height about log₂ n, so O(log n) comparisons. Degenerate tree (sorted insertion): height n, so O(n).
In-order sorts the keys; pre-order copies a tree; post-order deletes a tree or evaluates an expression tree.
